QQQ's 22% trailing-decade pace turns $100,000 into $1 million by 52, but the fund's lifetime 11% rate pushes that milestone to age 63.

QQQ holds zero financial stocks while NVIDIA, Apple, and Micron dominate its top holdings, leaving the fund fully exposed to any mega-cap tech downturn.

A lump-sum investor earns no dollar-cost averaging benefit, making consistent contributions a more controllable retirement lever than chasing an extra point of return.

Read More: Learn 7 secret wealth tips high net worth investors use that most investors miss (sponsor)

A 40-year-old drops $100,000 into QQQ, never adds another dollar, and reaches $1 million by 52. That is the arithmetic if Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) repeats its trailing decade at a roughly 22% annualized NAV return.

DesignRage / Shutterstock.com

QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100, a nondiversified basket of the 100 largest non-financial companies on the exchange. The same issuer reports a since-inception NAV return of about 11%, which pushes the same $1 million checkpoint to age 63, and an 8% assumption pushes it to 70.

This piece uses QQQ's own numbers to show why a growth investor likely needs a savings rate that does not depend on an exceptional decade repeating itself.

A Scenario Priced Off One Decade

At roughly a 22% annualized NAV return with distributions reinvested, a $100,000 lump sum passes $1 million in about 12 years. For a 40-year-old, that lands at age 52.

Swap in QQQ's roughly 11% since-inception figure and the first full-year checkpoint slides to age 63. Apply a plainer 8%, and the wait stretches to age 70.

QQQ trades near $705, up roughly 501% over the past ten years. That is the run being extrapolated, and it does not repeat by rule.

Why the Next Decade May Not Rhyme

The Nasdaq-100 is concentrated by design. QQQ's largest positions include NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) at about 8%, Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) near 7%, and Micron (NASDAQ:MU) at 6%, with Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), AMD (NASDAQ:AMD), and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) each in the 4% range. Semiconductors carry an unusual share of the fund because the index excludes financials by construction. If AI capex normalizes or memory pricing rolls over, the ETF has no bank or insurer earnings to cushion the drop.

title: S&P 500 Gets Fresh Warning From 5% Treasury Yield
detail:
S&P 500 Gets Fresh Warning From 5% Treasury Yield
Moz Farooque ACCA
Thu, September 17, 2026 at 12:26 PM MDT 2 min read
^GSPC
QQQ
Trade QQQ on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

The 10-year Treasury yield is hovering just below 5%, putting the S&P 500 near a level that has historically produced some of the market's weakest forward returns.

The benchmark yield eased about seven basis points Thursday morning to roughly 4.95%, after recently moving through a level last seen on a closing basis in 2007.

Is QQQ fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

That 5% threshold matters because history suggests stocks have struggled to generate their usual follow-through when Treasury yields remain that high.

Bespoke Investment Group data show that when the 10-year yield has traded with a 5-handle, the S&P 500 has gained just 0.4% on average over the following three months, with positive returns 56% of the time.

Six-month returns averaged 1.3%, while one-year gains averaged 4.1%.

Those figures compare with much stronger long-term averages of 2.2% over three months, 4.4% over six months and 9.1% over one year.

The historical pattern is not a guarantee of falling stocks.

Higher yields can coexist with equity gains if earnings growth and liquidity remain strong enough to absorb higher borrowing costs. But a 5% Treasury yield reduces the relative attractiveness of stocks because investors can earn more from lower-risk government bonds.

It also compresses the equity risk premium, making stretched valuations harder to justify.

Investors Takeaway

The key question is whether the 10-year yield can remain above 5% rather than simply touching the level.

Thursday's pullback to around 4.95% leaves that question unresolved. A sustained move above 5% would make the weaker historical return pattern more relevant.

For investors, that does not automatically mean selling stocks.

It does mean the hurdle for equities becomes higher. Earnings may need to remain strong enough to offset more attractive bond yields, while richly valued parts of the market could become increasingly sensitive to any disappointment.

History suggests 5% is less a crash signal than a warning that the easy part of the equity rally may be over.

Goldman's Nasdaq-100 put-call skew hit zero for only the 5th time in 20 years, with all prior instances preceding strong tech rallies.

Each of the 4 prior zero readings occurred during powerful AI-driven advances, not at market tops, signaling confidence rather than complacency.

The gauge dropped 0.25 points since March 2026, marking one of its largest 6-month declines on record, while Nasdaq-100 implied volatility also fell sharply.

Read More: Avoid these 13 retirement mistakes before they derail your future (sponsor)

Markets have rewarded technology leadership for much of the past several years. The Nasdaq-100 has climbed on AI investment, resilient earnings from mega-cap growth companies, and investors' willingness to pay for future growth.

Now, a Goldman Sachs options gauge tracking one-month put-call skew across Nasdaq-100 stocks has hit zero -- just the fifth time in 20 years, based on data going back to September 2006.

That level of calm is rare. All five instances have only occurred since the start of the AI era: once in late 2023, twice in 2024, and once earlier this year. Each occurred as technology stocks were beginning or continuing strong rallies.

What Put-Call Skew Measures

Put-call skew essentially shows how much investors are willing to pay for downside protection compared with upside bets.

Puts function like insurance against a market decline, while calls offer exposure to further gains. Normally, investors pay more for puts because protecting against losses is more valuable than betting on additional gains. That creates a positive skew reading.

When the average one-month skew across Nasdaq-100 stocks falls to zero, puts and calls are roughly equal in cost. Investors are no longer paying a meaningful premium for protection. Goldman's long-term average is about 0.11, making zero an unusually low reading.

In other words, options traders are showing unusually little fear. That can signal confidence -- or complacency. It does not predict the market's next move, but it does show that investors are pricing in relatively little downside risk.

Technology

The State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) advanced 1.5%, the iShares US Technology ETF (IYW) was 0.9% higher, and the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM) was inactive. Among semiconductor ETFs, the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) gained 1.5%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) rose by 2.4%.

Vicor (VICR) shares were up more than 12% in premarket activity after the company said it granted a nonexclusive license to a new AI original equipment manufacturer licensee with the right to procure Vertical Power Delivery modules covered by company patents from unlicensed suppliers.

Financial

The State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) advanced 0.4%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X Shares (FAS) was up 1.4%, while its bearish counterpart, Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X Shares (FAZ), was 1.4% lower.

Affirm (AFRM) shares were up 5% after the company said it launched a new transformer-based underwriting model that is now live at checkout in the US.

Health Care

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) advanced 0.1%, the Vanguard Health Care Index Fund (VHT) was up 0.7%, while the iShares US Healthcare ETF (IYH) was inactive. The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) was 0.3% higher.

IDEXX Laboratories (IDXX) stock was up more than 1% premarket after the company said it has expanded its Faecal Dx antigen testing platform in the UK to detect taeniid tapeworms, including Taenia and Echinococcus species.

Consumer

The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) was up 0.1%, the Vanguard Consumer Staples Index Fund ETF Shares (VDC) was down 0.1%, and the iShares US Consumer Staples ETF (IYK) was inactive. The State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) gained 0.8%. The VanEck Retail ETF (RTH) was inactive, while the State Street SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT) advanced 0.6%.

Nike (NKE) stock were 1.5% higher after the company said late Wednesday that Alexandre Arnault has been appointed to its board.

Commodities

Front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil retreated by 2.3% to $100.11 per barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange. Natural gas was down 0.4% at $2.88 per 1 million British Thermal Units. The United States Oil Fund (USO) decreased by 2.3%, while the United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was 0.3% lower.

Gold futures for November retreated by 0.1% to $4,385.30 an ounce on the Comex. Silver futures gained by 0.3% to reach $65.09 an ounce. SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) was up by 2.3%, and the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) rose by 3.4%.
